extracted.intended_audience: applicants, PD/PIs, trainees, and institutional grants administrators for NIH Kirschstein-NRSA and K (career development) awards
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for administration, conduct, reporting, payback, and eligibility for Ruth L. Kirschstein NRSA institutional training grants and NIH research career development (K) awards. Includes publication/copyright rules, human subjects/animals, payback rules, and specific K-program eligibility and mentor requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publications and sharing of research results
rubrics_metrics.description: PD/PIs and trainees should make the results and accomplishments of their Kirschstein-NRSA institutional training grant activities available to the research community and to the public at large; the recipient organization should assist trainees in these activities; no restrictions should be placed on the publication of results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trainees are encouraged to submit reports to journals of their choice; responsibility for direction of the project should not be ascribed to NIH. Information on trainee publications is included as part of the annual progress report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgment of NIH support in publications
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH IC support must be acknowledged by a footnote in language similar to: 'This investigation was supported by the National Institutes of Health under Ruth L. Kirschstein National Research Service Award (number) from the (name of NIH IC).'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also follow federal funding acknowledgment requirements provided in Appropriation Mandates—Acknowledgment of Federal Funding in IIA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Access Policy compliance for trainee-authored articles
rubrics_metrics.description: The Public Access Policy requirements described in Administrative Requirements—Availability of Research Results—NIH Public Access Policy in IIA apply to articles authored or co-authored by NRSA trainees and arising from NIH support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure manuscript submission and public access consistent with NIH Public Access Policy; track trainee publications in annual reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright of materials developed with NIH support
rubrics_metrics.description: When a publication or similar copyrightable material is developed from work supported by NIH, the author is free to arrange for copyright without the approval of the NIH awarding IC, except as otherwise provided in the NoA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any such copyrighted materials shall be subject to a royalty-free, nonexclusive, and irrevocable license to the Federal government to reproduce, translate, publish, and use and dispose of such materials, and to authorize others to do so for Federal government purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventions and patents for institutional training grants
rubrics_metrics.description: All Kirschstein-NRSA institutional research training grants and other funding agreements awarded primarily for educational purposes are not subject to invention reporting requirements nor does NIH have any rights to inventions under those grants and agreements (as specified in 2 CFR 200.315 and in 37 CFR 401.1(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If different award types are involved, consult applicable statutes/regulations; institutional policies may still apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition of professional fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees resulting from clinical practice, professional consultation, or other comparable activities performed pursuant to the purpose of the award may not be retained by the trainee and must be assigned to the recipient organization for disposition in accordance with NIH policy on program income.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term 'professional fees' does not apply to honoraria, fees for scholarly writing, occasional outside lectures, or advisory service to public/private non-profit organizations; if permitted by organizational policy, these fees may be retained by the trainee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with public policy requirements and appropriation mandates
rubrics_metrics.description: All Public Policy Requirements, Objectives, and Other Appropriation Mandates discussed in IIA apply to Kirschstein-NRSA Institutional programs when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must comply with policies governing civil rights; protection of human subjects (including data and safety monitoring and inclusion policies); humane care and use of vertebrate animals; human embryonic stem cells; recombinant or synthetic nucleic acid research. See IIA and SF424 (R&R) Section 8 for application requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human subjects: indefinite involvement procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant organization has an approved FWA or assurance on file but plans for involvement of human subjects are indefinite at application, provide the assurance number; human subjects may not be involved until IRB approval or exemption certification has been submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If trainees will participate in research supported by other grants with completed IRB review or exemption designation, that review is sufficient provided the trainee's participation does not substantially modify the research. The recipient institution must ensure trainees receive proper training/education in human subjects research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate animals: indefinite involvement procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: If plans for involvement of vertebrate animals are indefinite but an Animal Welfare Assurance is on file with OLAW, indicate 'Yes' to involvement and include the Assurance number; vertebrate animals may not be involved until verification of IACUC approval has been submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If trainees participate in research supported by other grants with completed IACUC review, that review is sufficient if trainee participation does not substantially modify the research. Ensure trainees are enrolled in animal welfare training and occupational health/safety programs and properly supervised when working with live vertebrate animals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payback obligation: predoctoral vs postdoctoral recipients
rubrics_metrics.description: Predoctoral recipients incur no payback obligation; postdoctoral recipients incur a payback obligation for the first 12 months of Kirschstein-NRSA support (a Payback Agreement Form PHS 6031 is required for the initial 12-month postdoctoral support period).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 13th and subsequent months of postdoctoral NRSA-supported research serve to pay back the obligation month by month. Short-term predoctoral training does not incur payback; postdoctoral short-term training does incur payback and accrues toward the first 12 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payback administration and determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon submission and acceptance of a Termination Notice, the NIH awarding IC determines if a payback obligation exists and forwards documents to the NIH Kirschstein-NRSA Payback Service Center (PSC), which administers payback activities and retains records until obligations are satisfied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PSC personnel are NIH experts in Kirschstein-NRSA payback requirements; the Chief, Kirschstein-NRSA PSC has delegated authority for payback matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service payback: definition of research
rubrics_metrics.description: Research is defined as activity involving designing experiments, developing protocols, and collecting and interpreting data; review of original research or administration of original research that includes providing scientific direction and guidance may be acceptable if a doctoral degree and relevant research experience is required for the position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research can be conducted in academic, government, for-profit, or other environments domestically or abroad. Analytic or technical activities conducted in direct support of research may also satisfy service payback when consistent with the individual's experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service payback: definition of teaching
rubrics_metrics.description: Teaching is an instructional activity in an organized educational or other instructional environment and generally carried out in a formal didactic setting; other activities may be considered if consistent with the certifying institution's policy on teaching responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When calculating hours of teaching per week, it is permissible to include 3 hours of preparation time for each hour of direct instruction. Acceptable teaching activities must have biomedical or health-related relevance and can take place at universities, schools, research institutes, hospitals, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service payback: definition of health-related
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Health-related' means related to the description, diagnosis, prevention, or treatment of disease; fields other than those usually considered directly related to human disease (e.g., agriculture, environmental sciences, biotechnology, bioengineering) also will be considered health-related.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation may consider the relation of the activity to health/disease and the cumulative type, amount, and frequency of experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time commitment requirement for service payback
rubrics_metrics.description: All acceptable payback activities must be undertaken for periods that average at least 20 hours per week; total employment averaging less than 20 hours per week cannot be counted except in cases of disability or other pressing personal/family circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If less than 20 hours/week is permitted, the total period of service obligation will be prorated (e.g., 12-month obligation at 10 hours/week becomes 24 months); such exceptions are rare and require prior approval from the PSC. Full-time employees may not engage in payback activities at effort levels below 20 hours/week.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiation of payback service options
rubrics_metrics.description: Postdoctoral payback may be discharged by receiving an equal number of months of postdoctoral Kirschstein-NRSA support beginning in the 13th month, or by engaging in an equal number of months of health-related research, research training, or teaching (or combination) that averages more than 20 hours per week.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Either route must meet the time and subject-matter requirements described for acceptable service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source of funding for service payback activities
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no restriction on the source of funds supporting an individual's service payback activity; support may come from a PHS grant, any non-Kirschstein-NRSA Federal or non-Federal source, and unpaid service is permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentations of activities will be evaluated by PSC for acceptability regardless of funding source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing to begin service obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual must begin to undertake the payback service requirement within 2 years after the termination date of Kirschstein-NRSA support unless an extension of time has been approved by the PSC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions of the 2-year initiation period may be requested via the Annual Payback Activities Certification form (APAC); valid plans to initiate soon after the grace period may justify an extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial payback: policy and principal calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: If an individual does not perform payback service, the Federal government may recover certain costs; the amount depends on when support was received and calculation formulas consider the total amount paid the individual (with specific definitions based on award type and sponsoring institution).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For institutional training grants or fellowships at domestic non-Federal sponsoring institutions, 'total paid' is stipend only; for foreign sponsoring institutions, includes round-trip travel; for Federal sponsoring institutions, includes institutional allowance expenditures (health insurance, travel, tuition, fees).

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial payback: interest and interest rate calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH computes interest on the principal amount beginning on the date the United States became entitled to recover stipends; interest rate is fixed by the Secretary of the Treasury considering prevailing rates; interest is computed on a 360-day year basis and applied through the date of receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interest may accrue after the 2-year grace period expires, deferment expiration, or if service terminates before completion. Applicable interest rate and the start of the 3-year repayment period depend on dates associated with voluntary vs involuntary payback accounts; repayment of amounts determined from the Termination Notice plus interest shall be paid within the 3-year period following such date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of payback and break in service: allowable bases
rubrics_metrics.description: The PSC may extend the period for undertaking payback service or permit breaks in continuous service based on specific criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria include necessity to complete non-health-related research or clinical training; participation in the NIH Loan Repayment Program (LRP); temporary disability; or substantial hardship where failure to extend would be against equity and good conscience. Examples: completing residency where clinical teaching/research not integral, seeking employment that would fulfill payback requirements. Participation in LRP defers NRSA obligation automatically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver policy and waiver criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH may waive, in whole or in part, the payback obligation upon determining compliance is impossible or would involve substantial hardship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests must be in writing to the PSC and include explanation per criteria: permanent and total disability will make compliance impossible; substantial hardship will be evaluated considering current and future financial resources and obligations; in rare cases consider reasons for failure to complete requirements, extent of payback activities performed, sufficiency of training, lack of employment opportunities, or other extenuating circumstances. Death cancels any payback obligation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification of payback activities (APAC PHS 6031-1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Payback service is certified through the Kirschstein-NRSA APAC; individuals with outstanding obligations must complete an APAC annually until obligation is fulfilled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An APAC is sent approximately one year after completion of support; forms must be returned within 30 days of the reporting period end date. PSC reviews forms, determines acceptability, and informs the individual of status. Any change of mailing address must be reported promptly to the PSC until discharge of obligation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breaks in NRSA support and APAC handling
rubrics_metrics.description: If a trainee/fellow has a period of non-Kirschstein-NRSA support between awards, appropriate activity performed during the period may count toward payback; if the nonsupport period is 6 months or longer, the individual receives an APAC automatically; if break is less than 6 months, an APAC will not be mailed automatically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If acceptable payback service was performed during a short break (<6 months), the individual may obtain and complete an APAC from the NIH web site to report service.

rubrics_metrics.name: NHSC scholars: separate service commitments
rubrics_metrics.description: Kirschstein-NRSA recipients who also have been National Health Service Corps (NHSC) scholars are required to fulfill their NHSC service commitment through direct clinical service to the underserved per NHSC policy; any Kirschstein-NRSA payback must be fulfilled separately through acceptable Kirschstein-NRSA service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume NHSC service satisfies NRSA payback; document separately to both programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective of research career development (K) awards
rubrics_metrics.description: The objective of NIH career development programs is to help ensure highly trained scientists are available to address biomedical, behavioral, and clinical research needs by providing mentored or independent experiences and protected time to develop research careers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentored programs provide supervised career development with goal of research independence; independent programs foster outstanding scientists to expand significant contributions; review NOFO and K Kiosk for program-specific details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types and general terms of individual mentored CDAs
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual mentored CDAs (e.g., K01, K07, K08, K22, K23, K25, K99/R00) provide protected time generally 3–5 years for intensive research career development under an experienced mentor; mentored CDAs are not renewable nor transferable from one individual to another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No-cost extensions in time are permitted but all terms and conditions remain during extension; applicants should consult parent NOFOs and IC-specific NOFOs for program requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor requirements for individual mentored CDAs
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications require the candidate to identify a primary mentor/sponsor with extensive and appropriate research experience who, together with the candidate, is responsible for planning, direction, and execution of the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The mentor should be recognized in the proposed research area, have a track record of success in training independent investigators, and have sufficient independent research support to cover proposed research costs in excess of allowable CDA costs. Co-mentors/sponsors may be included as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career transition awards (K22 and K99/R00) structure
rubrics_metrics.description: K22 generally supports a mentored phase followed by an independent phase (total up to 5 years); K99/R00 provides up to 2 years mentored (K99) and up to 3 years independent (R00) contingent on securing an independent research position and IC administrative review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some programs support only the independent phase; specific IC eligibility and award provisions vary and no parent NOFO exists for some K22 programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: K99/R00 eligibility: postdoctoral experience limits and extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: K99/R00 applicants must not have more than 4 years of postdoctoral research training as of the application due date; NIH will consider requests for extension of the eligibility window for reasons including medical concerns, disability, family care, extended clinical training, natural disasters, and active duty military service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH will approve an extension of one year for childbirth within the 4-year K99 eligibility window; applicants requesting this must provide the child's date of birth in the extension request justification to IC program officials at least 12 weeks before submitting an application.

rubrics_metrics.name: K99 phase rules on duration, early transition, and no-cost extension
rubrics_metrics.description: The K99 phase is generally for 2 years but recipients may transition earlier when offered an acceptable position; early transition is a prior approval request subject to NIH approval. No-cost extensions for K99 are not automatic and require prior NIH approval; all award terms remain during extensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When requesting a no-cost extension, submit a plan for continued career development and timely transition; if R00 application with a suitable position is not submitted within the one-year no-cost extension, the R00 will not be awarded. Carryover from K99 to R00 may be allowed if K99 was extramural-funded—consult the awarding IC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition to R00 phase: position and review requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: To transition to the R00 phase, the K99 recipient is required to secure a tenure-track, full-time assistant professor position or equivalent; transition is not guaranteed and the transition application is administratively reviewed by the awarding IC (not peer reviewed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There should not be a delay between K99 and R00 phases; R00 recipients are expected to compete successfully for independent R01 support during the R00.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual non-mentored (independent) CDA eligibility and terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Independent CDAs (e.g., K02, K05, K07 leadership, K24) provide protected time for scientists who can demonstrate the need for intensive research focus; candidates must have a doctoral degree and independent, peer-reviewed support at the time the award is made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some ICs require candidates to have an NIH research grant at application time; planning, direction, and execution of the program are the responsibility of the applicant and sponsoring institution. Independent CDAs are not transferable and may be renewable in some cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional scientist development programs (K12 and KL2) rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The K12 and KL2 provide institutional support for development of independent basic or clinical scientists (scholars) selected by the institution; a specified number of scholar positions are awarded in a K12 and K12 is solicited only by IC-specific NOFOs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: K12 is subject to NIH Standard Terms of Award; carryover of unobligated balances from one budget period generally requires prior written approval. K12 awards are generally not transferable. KL2 activity code used when part of a CTSA consortium. K30 supports clinical research curriculum development at the institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible institutions for CDAs
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for CDAs may be submitted on behalf of the candidate by any domestic for-profit or non-profit public or private institution/organization (e.g., universities, colleges, hospitals, laboratories) to support a research program in specified areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreign organizations are not eligible to apply for CDAs, but foreign components may apply. Consult specific NOFO for IC practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible individuals for CDAs and PD/PI rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Any individual with the skills, knowledge, and resources necessary to carry out the proposed research as the candidate (PD/PI) may apply with their organization; individuals from all backgrounds are encouraged to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple PD/PI applications are not accepted for individual CDAs; institutional CDAs should check the NOFO for allowability of Multiple PD/PIs. Review IC-specific NOFO and contact scientific/research or grants management contacts for eligibility clarifications.
